newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bank sees Argentina brady bond profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bank sees Argentina brady bond profit-taking.

text.p: Swiss private bank Union Bancaire Privee forecast more profit-taking in Argentina Brady bonds, saying charges of government corruption were scaring investors.
In a commentary on Argentina, the Geneva bank warned that investor fears about the country's political risk could be more harmful to the bond market than a slow resumption of growth.

Argentina's former economy minister Domingo Cavallo has whipped up a political storm since his sacking in July by accusing two senior ministers and President Carlos Menem's top aide of covering up corruption. They deny the allegations.

"Recent procrastination over the fiscal deficit sparked profit-taking in the bond market. This attitude has hardened and may well persist until the end of the year. The political instability generated by Cavallo's accusations of government corruption is the main cause," Union Bancaire Privee said.

The bank said investors were confident about Argentina's economic programme in the medium- and long-term and perceived only a moderate risk, but warned the bond market remained sensitive to political troubles in the next six months.
It forecast the yield differential between government paper and U.S. Treasury bonds to shrink by 250 basis points in 1997.

The bank said it favoured Mexican and Brazilian shares with better earnings growth prospects over Argentina. It said the Argentina stock market was trading at 12.5 times estimated 1997 earnings, which it forecast to rise by less than five percent.
